# B. Logic findings

### B2 (Major, live): job-overlap shift not chronological for multi-establishment workers

Status
:   Fixed 2026-07-07

Files
:   1. IRP5HHI.rmd
        * "fraction affected for all years" (4) — L215-218

Concern
:   * `shift()` follows physical row order; the key sorts by *place first*, date second
    * a person-firm group spanning >1 `busmainplc_geo` gets a `DateStart2` that is not the chronologically next job
    * `DJobDurationMonth` / `TDurationMonth` / `DoubleJobRatio` are then wrong for exactly the multi-establishment workers the block targets

Proposed fix
:   `setkey(ipyrc, Txrf, UID, DateStart)` immediately before the two `shift()` lines (taxyear is constant inside the year loop); re-set the original key after if later code relies on it

Cost
:   one extra sort per year loop (seconds); values change only for multi-place person-firm-years

Applied
:   2026-07-07 — key replaced, original commented with `#### CLAUDE tpo:`; server re-run required for values to change

```{=html}
<details><summary>show chunk excerpt — "fraction affected for all years" (4), L215-218</summary>
<pre>
 215:   setkey(ipyrc, busmainplc_geo, taxrefno, UID, DateStart)
 216:   #### DateStart2, DateEnd2: Dates for 2nd job in the same firm
 217:   ipyrc[, DateStart2 := shift(DateStart, n = 1L, type = "lead"), by = .(Txrf, taxyear, UID)]
 218:   ipyrc[,   DateEnd2 := shift(DateEnd, n = 1L, type = "lead"), by = .(Txrf, taxyear, UID)]
</pre>
</details>
```

### B3 (Major, live): masked-display line errors at runtime (`with = F` scope)

Status
:   Fixed 2026-07-07

Files
:   1. IRP5HHI.rmd
        * "define irp5M by location granularity" (16) — L999-1004

Concern
:   * with `with = F`, `j` is evaluated in the calling scope: `Txrf` is not an object there → "object 'Txrf' not found"
    * even if it resolved, the letter strings would be treated as (nonexistent) column names

Proposed fix
:   select real columns first, then add masked display columns: `x <- unique(irp5[cond, c("Txrf", "UID", geovars, grepout("Num|Rows|Gran|Commo", colnames(irp5))), with = F]); x[, Firm := letters[as.integer(factor(Txrf))]][, ind := letters[as.integer(factor(UID))]][, c("Txrf", "UID") := NULL]; x`

Applied
:   2026-07-07 — rewritten as `irp5msk` two-step msk pattern, original commented

```{=html}
<details><summary>show chunk excerpt — "define irp5M by location granularity" (16), L999-1004</summary>
<pre>
 999: unique(irp5[Txrf %in% Txrf[grepl("^M", LocGranularFirm) | grepl("^M", CommonLocality)][1]
1000:   & taxyear == 2009,
1001:   c(Firm = letters[as.integer(as.factor(Txrf))],
1002:   ind = letters[as.integer(as.factor(UID))],
1003:   geovars, grepout("Num|Rows|Gran|Commo", colnames(irp5))), with = F]
1004: )
</pre>
</details>
```

### B6 (Minor, live): plot outlier drop keeps establishments with extreme rows

Status
:   Fixed 2026-07-07

Files
:   1. IRP5Impacts.rmd
        * "examining estimation data" (7) — L337-338

Concern
:   * an establishment qualifies if **any** of its rows is moderate — its extreme rows are still plotted
    * the winsorize block, "select winsorized estimation sample" (11) L696-700, uses the correct exclusion idiom

Proposed fix
:   `lfdata[!(EstID %in% EstID[abs(rJobsMP) >= 200 | dJobsMP <= -1000]), ]`

# D. Refactor proposals

### D1 (non-drastic, spl): fold the 20 near-identical `feols()` calls into one explicit loop

Status
:   Open — apply when next editing the file

Files
:   1. IRP5Impacts.rmd
        * "estimation with winsorized data" (14) — L1079-1144, ×20
        * "estimation with various Job0 and start year" (9) — L518-543, same pattern ×8

Current
:   20 copies of the same formula/vcov differing only in `data =`

Proposed
:   named list of subsets + a plain `for` loop (no function wrapping; errors stay explicit):

```{r}
subsets <- list(
    "All sample"                               = LfYr
  , "Complete panel"                           = LfCYr
  , "Existed firms, all sample"                = LfCEYr
  , "Existed firms, high concentrated markets" = LfCEaYr
  , "Existed firms, low concentrated markets"  = LfCEbYr
  , "Existed firms, low FA"   = LfCEYr[grepl("low", FAclass), ]
  , "Existed firms, mid FA"   = LfCEYr[grepl("mid", FAclass), ]
  , "Existed firms, high FA"  = LfCEYr[grepl("hi",  FAclass), ]
  #### ... size and size-x-HHI subsets in the same style
)
eslistYrw <- vector("list", length(subsets))
names(eslistYrw) <- names(subsets)
for (k in seq_along(subsets))
  eslistYrw[[k]] <- feols(
    rJobsMP ~ i(taxyear, Pre2013FAMP0, ref = 2012) |
      taxyear + taxrefno + busmainplc_geo,
    vcov = ~ taxyear + busmainplc_geo,
    data = subsets[[k]])
```

Gain
:   ~120 lines → ~30; one place to edit the spec; removes the copy-paste channel that produced B7. No speed change

### D2 (record only — intentional): qsave→qread ALTREP round trips

Status
:   Closed — deliberate memory optimisation; do not "simplify" away

Files
:   1. IRP5HHI.rmd
        * "faa and Fadata are first lines of FAD in each year" (7) — L504-506
        * "LSa is LS of agri only" (20) — L1274-1276
        * analogues elsewhere in the file

What
:   * saving then immediately re-reading with `use_alt_rep = TRUE` converts in-memory string columns to ALTREP and cuts RAM on the 100M-row tables

Proposed
:   add a `#### CLAUDE com:` marker at each so future scans skip them

```{=html}
<details><summary>show chunk excerpt — "faa and Fadata..." (7), L504-506</summary>
<pre>
 504: qsave(Fadata, paste0(pathdata, "FAFirstRow.qs"), nthreads = DTThreads)
 505: Fadata <- qread(paste0(pathdata, "FAFirstRow.qs"),
 506:   nthreads = DTThreads, use_alt_rep = TRUE)
</pre>
</details>
```

# Scanner residue

What "not name-checkable (`...` in formals)" means:

* the scanner validates each named argument in a call against `formals(pkg::fn)` of the installed package
* if a function's formals contain `...`, R accepts **any** argument name without error — an unknown name is silently absorbed into `...`
* a name check therefore proves nothing for such functions; the scanner skips them and only counts them
* in this project that is ~700 calls across ~56 functions: `feols`, `ggplot`, `aes`, `theme`, `data.table()`, `paste`, `etable`, `tt`, `style_tt`, `merge`, `dcast`, ...
* C6 (`geom_pointrange(width=)`) is a real mistake living exactly in this blind spot — ggplot warns at run time, nothing errors
* for these functions the rule falls back to the help page: confirm in `?fn` that the argument is actually consumed

Other residue:

* unresolved symbols: `.` (data.table alias, expected), `county_rain` (hurricaneexposure not installed — COVIDDealths.rmd only)
* packages not installed on this machine: hurricaneexposuredata, hurricaneexposure
